Question: Chrome/Edge started by the parity tool showed no page tree (0 lines); how to get a real read?
Choice: Launch Chrome/Edge with --disable-features=CalculateNativeWinOcclusion --disable-backgrounding-occluded-windows and Firefox with widget.windows.window_occlusion_tracking.enabled=false (throwaway profiles only)
Why: Measured: a window opened behind others is occluded; Chromium builds no accessibility tree (even with --force-renderer-accessibility) and Firefox marks the front page offscreen. A user reads a page in front, so this reproduces the real condition.

Question: Where do fixture docs and the background-tab filter come from, and what about W1-6's ineffective node filter?
Choice: Fixtures from key_probe.read_keys (control+raw) + key_probe._typed; read_keys filters Documents by the CACHED IsOffscreen. core/ untouched (rule 6): the read_page_nodes filter bug goes to W2-5
Why: key_probe's node fields are the fixture format; onscreen_only's CurrentIsOffscreen raises on AutomationElementMode_None elements so every Document is kept. W1-7 is not allowed to change SGT capture.

Question: Service settings, on save: Sera shows 'will watch gst-like.gov.in for <service>' (D21). If the user answers No, what happens? A = nothing is saved, the edit dialog stays open so the link can be changed. B = the service is saved but its domain is not watched (Sera remembers this choice per service in a synced setting).
Which services overlap rules apply when registering portals?
Choice: A domain equal to or covering/under Income Tax or GST is not registered (built-in wins); a domain overlapping one an earlier service (sort order) claimed is skipped; extra_domains only for portal names that are services; a single-label host gives no domain
Why: no duplicate portals for one domain; narrowest scope; built-ins stay untouched

Question: Part N: what counts as a value vote for a link position?
Choice: each distinct client once (VALUE_CLIENTS = 3, page votes 0), not each link pair
Why: R8: link-pair counting let 2 clients with 3 sibling pages mask a position, while many clients sharing 2 years never did; 3 keeps W1-4's tested 2-clients-not-enough / 3-clients-masked behaviour

Question: Part D: rarity weight of a value both compared captures show
Choice: count the compared pair as one capture: 1 / (rarity - 1)
Why: an equal value is always shown by both, an unequal one by one; literal 1/rarity halved agreement, so one changed value among 10 rare ones gave 0.82 (undecided) instead of 0.9 (same); blueprint says an ARN weighs 1

Question: Part D check: the two fictional local-page sessions should be one client
Why: counts on today's captures: per page 3 codes, 2 periods and 1 alphanumeric value differ (sim 0.70, was 0.56): not one client; the blueprint's expectation was wrong, undecided is the honest result (rule 6)

Question: How does memory match rejected signatures?
Choice: (link, shape, text) matching either self.link or self.page
Why: Allows callers to pass either resolved base link or page string cleanly

Question: Edge window title with profile name: strip only the zero-width space, or also the profile segment?
Choice: Allow zero-width spaces inside 'Microsoft Edge' in BROWSER_SUFFIX_RE only
Why: Chrome/Edge titles must not change; the leftover '- Profile 1' is stable and only used when the address bar is unreadable

Question: How to key Firefox-only line rules (dropdown options, doubled label)?
Choice: On the Document's framework id 'Gecko' (live CurrentFrameworkId / cached 30024); node trees carry gecko:true on the document's first node
Why: Blueprint rule: browser-dependent rules key on framework id; Chrome/Edge lines and nodes stay byte-identical

Question: Retirement follows time order, so forward/reversed builds can legitimately differ once 4+ clients exist; how is 'orders agree' kept meaningful?
Choice: The order check builds both orders with retire=False (PageMemory/build retire flag); the runner prints 'retired (time order): k' from the forward build
Why: Part H counts misses in a row by time; the order check is meant to prove alignment and verdicts do not depend on client order

Question: Part C rule 2 'changes with time': does a day seen by only one client count as agreement?
Choice: No: the texts must differ between days that 2+ clients were seen on
Why: Rule 6: two clients captured on different days with their own data would otherwise be called noise and their datapoint lost

Question: Which verdicts may a label candidate come from, given probably furniture asks for labels while verdicts are being computed?
Choice: Base verdict 'same for all clients' with a fixable or alphanumeric type, plus unpaired repeats of such a (shape, text)
Why: Same set as compare.py's fixed + variable_alignment + semi-variable alphanumeric (variable_alignment only ever comes from a fixable text); avoids the label -> verdict -> furniture -> label loop

Question: A node in a real table whose column has no name (or a header cell): what label?
Choice: Fall back to the screen-box rules (labels._label, which still tries the structural _table_label first)
Why: Blueprint: box rules apply to values outside any table and to tables without table markup; a nameless column gives the table nothing to say

Question: How do container moves reach suggest()?
Choice: moves={key: class} argument; override with reason 'moved by the user'
Why: sdis_decisions table does not exist before W4-4; the dict is what that reader will pass
